messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I want a fair financial share, and I’m not agreeing to subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I don’t want to hurt my twin, but I haven’t given permission. I’d like us to settle it fairly, without rushing.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. Building financial independence matters to me.
Thank you. I’d like my share of the estate to help me start a dance studio. Having some money of my own would mean a lot to me. I’m not sure yet what that means for the house or what the shares are.

I’d change (1) to: “I want a fair financial share, and I haven’t agreed to subsidize A’s discounted purchase.” (2) works as “I’d like this settled fairly, without rushing.” No other concerns right now.
Yes, that wording fits. Owning it with my husband would give us a home of our own. A family discount matters to me, though I don’t know what price or terms would be fair yet.
Yes, that mostly fits. I’d say I’d like clear information about the will and what may be available to me, so I can consider using it toward a dance studio.
Yes, that captures what matters to me. I’m not agreeing to any particular price or share.
Yes, that fits. I’d like us to take time to agree on fair terms.
No major discomfort. Getting the will and valuation shared sounds useful, as long as it doesn’t commit anyone to a decision.
No discomfort with getting the will and an independent valuation, as long as it’s shared with all three and commits no one to a decision.
